title: Interests
text:
While some of my interests intersect with our natural world, I have many other hobbies that I try to fit into my life when I have the time.

Surfing

I started surfing regularly in college and have fallen in love with the feeling of riding a wave. Surfing has been a great way for me to connect with the ocean, and take a break from my work. After all, you can’t bring your laptop out in the water! My favorite spots to surf around UCSB are Deveroux Point and Sands Beach. As a current longboarder I enjoy the slow rolling waves of Deveroux. Sands Beach isn’t always sandy despite the name, and can get pretty gnarly during the winter due to the larger swells and rocky bottoms. During the summer however, the swell mellows out and sand is returned to the bottom so it’s a fun place to catch lots of beach break waves with my friends.





Stand-Up Comedy

I have recently started performing stand-up comedy sets at open mics after having enjoyed watching shows for two years. Stand-up has brought a lot of joy to my life and I hope I can share it with other people through my performances. It has definitely challenged me to improve my public speaking skills beyond what is expected in a classroom. This includes proper timing talking in a dynamic voice, and putting myself in the vulnerable position of performing with people expecting me to be funny.





Video Games

I enjoy immersing myself in video games from time to time. Some of my favorite games are: The Outer Worlds, Skyrim, Sunset Overdrive, and playing Call of Duty Zombies with my friends.





Trying Out New Things

The photo above is not to show off any spectacular aptitude for ice skating but rather to provide an example of something I was trying for the first time. There is soo much to experience and learn in this world that I think it is limiting to put yourself into a box of what you do.
Some things I have been trying out include rock climbing, oragami, sketching with pen, and yoga.

title: About Me
text:
I grew up in Davis, California with my parents, sister, and maternal grandmother for a good part of my childhood. Growing up in Davis fostered a care for our planet and to consider the needs of people beyond myself.
Some of the major activities I engage with in my hometown were baseball, tennis, and playing the piano. Although I was reluctant to learn piano in my early years, it is now a skill I greatly appreciate.




My environmental origin story

The beginnings of my environmentalist journey showed my good intentions, but impractical solutions in retrospect. After a presentation on the drought that California was in, I took it to heart, and started taking in less water. This was because drinking water was one of the more tangible uses of water that I experienced on a day to day basis. This led to a lot of headaches, which I realize now were not a cost of a effective water conservation strategy.
Since then, I have learned about more effective strategies for water use reduction such as shorter showers in my own life, or for a societal scale, agricultural water use, and thermoelectric water use.





My future plans

At the beginning of college, figuring out what I wanted to do for work after college felt like fishing in the ocean. Now it is a bit better, with the body of water the size of a lake. What is certain is that I would like to work right after college to get a feel for what I really want to do, before considering returning to grad school.
I am open to doing any environmental work that helps the world but some areas of particular interest are habitat restoration, performing field impact analysis on the environment in consulting, water resources management, and sustainable agriculture.

title: Citrus Donations
text: The farm that I work at sells avocados commercially, but has about 40 citrus trees for the land owners and workers. While working at the farm I observed a significant amount of citrus was falling to the ground and rotting instead of making it to peoples mouths. Thus, I proposed and have implemented a donation program to deliver excess citrus to the UCSB Food Bank! Read more about my project and general citrus orchard care below.

title: Interactive Dashboard For White Buffalo Land Trust
text:
Over the 2025 summer I had the amazing opportunity to create an interactive dashboard for the White Buffalo Land Trust under the mentorship of Isa Elias, a Bren graduate student. The purpose of the dashboard was to provide an overhead view of daily conditions such as vegetation cover and soil moisture across different pastures on the White Buffalo Land Trust’s 1000 acre ranch. By comparing multiple pastures at a time, or comparing pastures between different times, this dashboard can help the land stewardship team decide where to move cattle to.
You can checkout the dashboard clicking here

title: Wind Projects
text:
For my GIS class I worked with a group of four others to determine potential suitable sites for wind turbines in Alabama. Finding a suitable site involved considering multiple factors such as proximity to human residencies, wind speed, and land use type. To generate a layer of suitable sites, my job was to develop a model builder to process the different layers and perform a raster calculator to highlight potential suitable sites.
You can scroll through our story map, which shows the context of our project and our results here

title: Hazardous Waste Impact on Low Birth Weight
text: Over the summer of 2024, I worked in a group with two other students under the mentorship of professors and graduate students to study an environmental justice issue. Our group decided to investigate how the number and proximity to hazardous waste sites impacts low birth weights. In this project we compared San Joaqin County, which experiences disproportional environmental pollution burden, and Santa Barbara County. Below you can see our presentation with out findings.

title: Arthropod Diversity Based on Interrow Plant Diversity in Coffee Farms
text:
While touring a farm in Costa Rica, the workers spoke about the difference in weeds between the farm that they managed organically by hand, and the other which they applied herbicide. I was curious as to how herbicide not only affected the prevalence of interrow plants, but also how the prevalance of interrow plants might affect the arthropod diversity and abundance.
